## merge day3 day5 data into one

```{r}
dc <- merge(d3, y = d5, add.cell.ids = c("d3", "d5"), project = "DC")
```

## redo analysis

```{r}
dc <- NormalizeData(dc)
# Select the top 1000 most variable features
dc <- FindVariableFeatures(dc, selection.method = "mean.var.plot")

# Scaling RNA data, we only scale the variable features here for efficiency
dc <- ScaleData(dc, features = VariableFeatures(dc))

# Run PCA
dc <- RunPCA(dc, features = VariableFeatures(dc))

# View PCA
VizDimLoadings(dc, dims = 1:4, reduction = "pca")

## In particular DimHeatmap allows for easy exploration of the primary sources of heterogeneity in a dataset, and can be useful when trying to decide which PCs to include for further downstream analyses. Both cells and features are ordered according to their PCA scores. Setting cells to a number plots the ‘extreme’ cells on both ends of the spectrum, which dramatically speeds plotting for large datasets. Though clearly a supervised analysis, we find this to be a valuable tool for exploring correlated feature sets.

DimHeatmap(dc, dims = 1:15, cells = 500, balanced = TRUE)
```

```{r}
ElbowPlot(dc, ndims = 40)
dc <- FindNeighbors(dc, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:29)
dc <- FindClusters(dc, resolution = 2, verbose = FALSE)
dc <- RunTSNE(dc, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:20)

# Projecting singlet identities on TSNE visualization
DimPlot(dc, group.by = "HTO_maxID")
```

## cell cycle scoring

__!NOTE__: variable `cc.genes` is loaded with `Seurat` library. They are all capital human genes. Convert to title capital first. Later we discovered 3 genes name are different between human and mouse. It was fixed in dc_v4.1.

```{r}
firstup <- function(x) {
  x <- tolower(x)
  substr(x, 1, 1) <- toupper(substr(x, 1, 1))
  x
}

s.genes <- firstup(cc.genes$s.genes)
g2m.genes <- firstup(cc.genes$g2m.genes)
dc <- CellCycleScoring(dc, s.features = s.genes, g2m.features = g2m.genes, set.ident = TRUE)

RidgePlot(dc, features = c("Pcna", "Top2a", "Mcm6", "Mki67"), ncol = 2)

FeaturePlot(dc, features = "Flt3", split.by = "HTO_maxID", ncol = 2)
```
```{r}
## Look at Phase distribution split by samples
DimPlot(dc, split.by = "HTO_maxID", group.by = "Phase")
```
```{r}
DimPlot(dc, split.by = "HTO_maxID", group.by = "Phase")
```

```{r}
## look at Signlech, a pDC marker
FeaturePlot(dc, features = "Siglech", split.by = "HTO_maxID", ncol = 2)
```
